sections.title: Things You Have
sections.content: You met this in Lesson 10 with age: Spanish has twenty-five years rather than being twenty-five. The same trick covers most of how you feel. Hunger, thirst, sleepiness, cold, heat, luck — all of them are things you have, not things you are. So 'tengo hambre', and never 'soy hambre' or 'estoy hambre'.

sections.title: With other people
rows: todos tenemos un poco de sueño

items.spanish: Yo también tengo sed. ¿Vamos a comer algo?
items.english: I'm thirsty too. Shall we go and eat something?

items.spanish: Después de esta mañana, todos tenemos un poco de sueño.
items.english: After this morning, we're all a little sleepy.
Are you cold? The window is open.

sections.content: Because these are nouns, 'very' is 'mucha' or 'mucho', not 'muy': 'tengo mucha hambre', 'tengo mucho sueño'. 'Muy' belongs with adjectives — 'estoy muy cansado'.
